name: Subhūti
summary: Disciple of the Buddha, foremost of those who dwell in peace (araṇāvihārin); in the Perfection of Wisdom sūtras he teaches the perfection of wisdom through the Buddha's power and is the Buddha's interlocutor in the Vajracchedikā, where he weeps on hearing it.

realization_account.text: An arhat declared foremost in dwelling without conflict; in the Vajracchedikā §9 he says he does not think 'I am an arhat free of passion'.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account (as a figure of the sūtras)

name: Avalokiteśvara
summary: The bodhisattva of compassion: in Lotus ch. 25 he rescues all who call his name from fire, water, bandits and bondage and takes whatever form will teach them (33 forms); he speaks the Heart Sūtra; in the Kāraṇḍavyūha he empties the hells and gives the six-syllable mantra; attendant of Amitābha in Sukhāvatī; in the Gaṇḍavyūha a spiritual friend on Mount Potalaka; in the Śūraṅgama his penetration through hearing is chosen as best. Guanyin, Kannon, Chenrezig.

realization_account.text: A great bodhisattva of the tenth ground, or a buddha of the past (Zhengfa Ming) appearing as a bodhisattva; his realization is the penetration of hearing into the self-nature (Śūraṅgama juan 6)
realization_account.label: the tradition's account (as a figure of the sūtras)

notes: Gender: male in Indian and Tibetan iconography; female forms (Guanyin) prevalent in East Asia from c. 10th c.

name: Mañjuśrī
summary: The bodhisattva of wisdom, 'ever-youthful' (kumārabhūta): visits Vimalakīrti and asks about non-duality; sends Sudhana on his pilgrimage and receives him at its end; teaches the Saptaśatikā; in the Lotus recalls the past buddha Candrasūryapradīpa and brings forth the nāga princess; in the Śūraṅgama chooses Avalokiteśvara's method.

realization_account.text: A bodhisattva who in the Śūraṅgamasamādhi-sūtra is revealed to have been a buddha in the past; Wutaishan in China is his abode (Chinese tradition).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account (as a figure of the sūtras)

name: Samantabhadra
summary: The bodhisattva of practice and vows: at the end of the Gaṇḍavyūha Sudhana enters his body and his vows of good conduct (Bhadracarī) conclude the text; in Lotus ch. 28 he rides a six-tusked white elephant to protect those who keep the sūtra; in Nyingma, Samantabhadra is also the name of the primordial buddha (a distinct usage).

name: Maitreya (the bodhisattva, future buddha)
summary: The bodhisattva who will be the next buddha, now in Tuṣita: in the Lotus he asks the questions that open the sūtra and receives the revelation of the Buddha's lifespan; in the Gaṇḍavyūha he opens the tower of Vairocana to Sudhana; in the Śālistamba he teaches dependent origination; in the Saṃdhinirmocana (ch. 8) he asks about calm and insight. Tibetan tradition makes him the teacher of Asaṅga and source of the five Maitreya treatises.
notes: Distinct from tch:maitreya (the Upaniṣadic sage). Same figure as tch:metteyya (U36, Pali form) — dedupe candidate for the merge. The treatise-author 'Maitreyanātha' of the scholarly account is tch:maitreyanatha.

name: Kṣitigarbha
summary: The bodhisattva of the earth-womb who vowed not to become a buddha until the hells are empty; protector of the dead, children and travellers in East Asia (Dizang, Jizō).

name: Mahāsthāmaprāpta
summary: The bodhisattva of great strength, attendant of Amitābha with Avalokiteśvara; object of the eleventh contemplation of the Contemplation Sūtra; in the Śūraṅgama his penetration is by recollection of the Buddha.

name: Ākāśagarbha
summary: The bodhisattva 'womb of space', before whom bodhisattvas confess root downfalls (Ākāśagarbha-sūtra); his mantra-recitation (gumonji) was practiced by Kūkai.

name: Vimalakīrti
summary: The Licchavi householder of Vaiśālī, a bodhisattva of inconceivable skillful means who lives as a layman, visits gambling halls and brothels to teach, feigns illness to draw the Buddha's disciples, and answers Mañjuśrī's question on non-duality with silence; he comes from Akṣobhya's world Abhirati.
alt_names: Dri ma med par grags pa

realization_account.text: Had served past buddhas, obtained the acceptance of dharmas, eloquence and dhāraṇī (Vimalakīrti 2.1)
realization_account.label: the tradition's account (as a figure of the sūtras)

name: Śrīmālā
summary: Queen of Ayodhyā, daughter of king Prasenajit and Mallikā, who in the Śrīmālā sūtra teaches the one vehicle and the tathāgatagarbha with the Buddha's confirmation; she receives the prediction that she will become the buddha Samantaprabha.

realization_account.text: Predicted to buddhahood as Samantaprabha (Śrīmālā ch. 1)
realization_account.label: the tradition's account (as a figure of the sūtras)

name: Sadāprarudita
summary: The 'Ever-Weeping' bodhisattva of Aṣṭasāhasrikā ch. 30-31, who searches for the perfection of wisdom, sells his own flesh and blood to honor the teacher Dharmodgata, and is tested by Śakra; model of devotion to the spiritual friend.

name: Dharmodgata
summary: The bodhisattva of the city Gandhavatī who teaches the perfection of wisdom to Sadāprarudita: the Tathāgatas neither come nor go, like a mirage (Aṣṭa ch. 31).
alt_names: Fashang 法上 / Tanwujie 曇無竭

name: Sudhana
summary: The merchant's son of the Gaṇḍavyūha who, sent by Mañjuśrī, visits over fifty spiritual friends, enters Maitreya's tower and merges with Samantabhadra; model of the seeker in one life (Huayan: the fifty-three stages).

name: Mahāmati
summary: The bodhisattva who asks the Buddha the 108 questions of the Laṅkāvatāra.

name: Vajragarbha (bodhisattva of the Daśabhūmika)
summary: The bodhisattva who, empowered by the buddhas, expounds the ten grounds in the Daśabhūmika.

name: Amitābha / Amitāyus
summary: The buddha of Immeasurable Light and Life who presides over Sukhāvatī in the west; as the monk Dharmākara he made the vows (48 in T360) to receive all who call on him.

realization_account.text: Awakened ten kalpas ago (Smaller & Larger Sukhāvatīvyūha)
realization_account.label: the tradition's account (as a figure of the sūtras)

name: Bhaiṣajyaguru Vaiḍūryaprabha
summary: The Medicine Buddha of the eastern land of lapis, whose twelve vows heal body and mind.

name: Akṣobhya
summary: The 'Immovable' buddha of the eastern world Abhirati, who as a monk vowed never to feel anger.

name: Prabhūtaratna
summary: The extinct buddha of the past whose stūpa rises from the earth in Lotus ch. 11 to hear the sūtra, and who shares his seat with Śākyamuni.

name: Dīpaṅkara
summary: The buddha of the distant past who predicted the future buddhahood of Śākyamuni (then the brahmin youth Sumedha / Megha); the Vajracchedikā says the Tathāgata received no dharma from him.

name: Sadāparibhūta
summary: The 'Never-Disparaging' bodhisattva of Lotus ch. 20, a past life of Śākyamuni, who bowed to everyone saying 'I do not disparage you, for you will all become buddhas' and was beaten for it.

name: Bhaiṣajyarāja
summary: The 'Medicine King' bodhisattva of the Lotus, who in a past life as Sarvasattvapriyadarśana burned his body as an offering to the buddha and the sūtra (Lotus ch. 23).

name: The daughter of the nāga king Sāgara
summary: The eight-year-old nāga princess of Lotus ch. 12, whom Mañjuśrī taught in the sea: she offers a jewel to the Buddha, and before Śāriputra's doubt about women's bodies she instantly becomes a male bodhisattva and a buddha in the southern world Vimalā.

name: Vaidehī
summary: Queen of Magadha, mother of Ajātaśatru, whose plea for a land without sorrow occasions the Contemplation Sūtra.

name: Akṣayamati
summary: The bodhisattva whose teaching on the inexhaustible qualities gives the Akṣayamatinirdeśa its name; in Lotus ch. 25 he asks about Avalokiteśvara.

name: Paramārthasamudgata
summary: The bodhisattva who, in Saṃdhinirmocana ch. 7, asks the intent of 'all dharmas lack own-being' and hears the three naturelessnesses and the three turnings.

name: Lokakṣema
summary: Kuṣāṇa monk in Luoyang (active c. 167-186) who made the first Chinese translations of Mahāyāna sūtras: the 8,000-line Perfection of Wisdom (Daoxing, 179), the Pratyutpanna-samādhi, the Akṣobhyavyūha, the Kāśyapaparivarta, the Śūraṅgamasamādhi (lost) and others.

name: Dharmarakṣa
summary: Yuezhi-descended monk of Dunhuang (c. 233-310) who translated the Lotus (286), the 25,000-line Perfection of Wisdom (Guangzan, 286), the Lalitavistara, the Daśabhūmika and many others.

name: Kumārajīva
summary: Kuchean monk-translator (344-413 or 350-409) in Chang'an, whose Chinese versions of the Lotus, Vimalakīrti, Diamond, Smaller Sukhāvatīvyūha, Large and Small Perfection of Wisdom, Śūraṅgamasamādhi, Mūlamadhyamakakārikā and the Dazhidu lun became standard in East Asia.
notes: Also referenced by other units; contribution here: sūtra translations.

name: Buddhabhadra
summary: Indian dhyāna master and translator (359-429) who with Faxian translated the six-fascicle Nirvāṇa Sūtra and alone the 60-fascicle Avataṃsaka (418-421) and the Tathāgatagarbha Sūtra.

name: Faxian
summary: Chinese pilgrim-monk (c. 337-422) who travelled to India and Sri Lanka and brought back the Mahāsāṃghika Vinaya and the Mahāyāna Nirvāṇa Sūtra, translated with Buddhabhadra (T376, 418).

name: Dharmakṣema
summary: Indian monk (385-433) in the Northern Liang capital Guzang who translated the 40-fascicle Mahāparinirvāṇa (421), the Golden Light, the Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka, the Mahāmegha and the Upāsakaśīla.

name: Guṇabhadra
summary: Indian monk (394-468) in Jiankang who translated the four-fascicle Laṅkāvatāra (443), the Śrīmālā (436), the Aṅgulimālīya and the Mahābherī; the early Chan 'Laṅkāvatāra masters' treated him as their first patriarch.

name: Bodhiruci (6th c.)
summary: North Indian monk in Luoyang (arrived 508) who translated the ten-fascicle Laṅkāvatāra, the Vajracchedikā, Vasubandhu's Daśabhūmika commentary and the Anūnatvāpūrṇatvanirdeśa.
notes: Distinct from the Tang translator Bodhiruci (d. 727) who compiled the Ratnakūṭa (T310).

name: Ratnamati
summary: Central Indian monk in Luoyang who translated the Ratnagotravibhāga into Chinese (T1611, 511) and, with Bodhiruci, Vasubandhu's Daśabhūmika commentary.

name: Paramārtha
summary: Indian monk (499-569) in southern China who translated Yogācāra and buddha-nature works (Mahāyānasaṃgraha, Foxing lun, and — by attribution — the Awakening of Faith).

name: Xuanzang
summary: Chinese pilgrim and translator (602-664) who studied at Nālandā and translated the 600-fascicle Mahāprajñāpāramitā, the Heart Sūtra (649), the Saṃdhinirmocana (647), the Vimalakīrti (650), the Bhaiṣajyaguru (650) and the Yogācārabhūmi; founder of the Faxiang tradition with Kuiji.

name: Śikṣānanda
summary: Khotanese monk (652-710) who translated the 80-fascicle Avataṃsaka (695-699) and the seven-fascicle Laṅkāvatāra; the Kṣitigarbha Pūrvapraṇidhāna Sūtra is attributed to him.

name: Prajña (translator of the 40-fascicle Avataṃsaka)
summary: Monk from Kapiśa (active 780s-810) who translated the 40-fascicle Gaṇḍavyūha (T293, 795-798), whose last fascicle gives Samantabhadra's ten great vows.

name: Pāramiti (Pramiti)
summary: Indian monk to whom the Chinese Śūraṅgama Sūtra (T945) is attributed as translator, at Guangzhou in 705; known only from the tradition's account.

name: Amoghavajra
summary: Esoteric master and translator (705-774) in Tang China who re-translated the Humane Kings sūtra and the Adhyardhaśatikā and many dhāraṇī texts.

name: Yijing
summary: Chinese pilgrim-monk (635-713) who translated the Golden Light (703), the Diamond and the Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya, and described Indian monastic life.

name: Yeshe De
summary: Tibetan translator (late 8th-early 9th c.) who, with Indian scholars such as Jinamitra, Surendrabodhi and Dānaśīla, translated a large part of the Mahāyāna sūtras into Tibetan.

name: Jinamitra
summary: Kashmiri paṇḍita in Tibet (late 8th-9th c.) who co-translated many sūtras and the Mahāvyutpatti terminology.

name: Sāramati
summary: Indian master to whom the Chinese tradition (Fazang and others) attributes the Ratnagotravibhāga; also named as author of the Dasheng fajie wuchabie lun.
notes: The Tibetan tradition attributes the RGV to Maitreya and Asaṅga; both attributions recorded on the source.

name: Aśvaghoṣa
summary: Buddhist poet (c. 1st-2nd c.) of the Buddhacarita and Saundarananda; the Awakening of Faith is traditionally attributed to him (doubted by scholars).
notes: Other units may add his poems; this entry contributes the attribution only.

name: Daosheng
summary: Chinese monk (c. 355-434), disciple of Kumārajīva, who taught that even icchantikas have buddha-nature and can become buddhas and that awakening is sudden, before the full Nirvāṇa Sūtra reached the south; expelled from the Jiankang saṅgha, he was vindicated when Dharmakṣema's version arrived containing that teaching.

realization_account.text: Chinese accounts say that on Tiger Hill the stones nodded when he preached that icchantikas have buddha-nature
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Tokuitsu
summary: Japanese Hossō monk (c. 780-842) who debated Saichō on whether the one vehicle or the three vehicles are final and whether all beings have buddha-nature (the 'three-one' controversy).

name: Saichō
summary: Founder of Japanese Tendai (767-822), who defended the Lotus's one vehicle and universal buddha-nature against Tokuitsu.
notes: Owned by U55 (Tendai); this entry contributes the debate with Tokuitsu.

name: Ngok Loden Sherab
summary: Tibetan translator (1059-1109) who translated the Ratnagotravibhāga with Sajjana and taught it in an 'analytic' tradition reading buddha-nature as emptiness, a non-affirming negation.

name: Gyaltsab Je
summary: Gyaltsab Darma Rinchen (1364-1432), Tsongkhapa's disciple and first successor at Ganden, author of the Gelug commentary on the Ratnagotravibhāga.
alt_names: rgyal tshab dar ma rin chen

name: Gö Lotsawa Zhönnu Pel
summary: Tibetan scholar (1392-1481), author of the Blue Annals and of a commentary on the Ratnagotravibhāga linking it with Mahāmudrā.
alt_names: 'gos lo tsā ba gzhon nu dpal

name: Rangjung Dorje (Third Karmapa)
summary: Third Karmapa (1284-1339), author of the Treatise on Buddha-Nature and of the Profound Inner Meaning; joined buddha-nature to Mahāmudrā.
